sentences.text:
THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:27.01.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.4679/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE XXII ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES & MEMBER, MACT,
BENGALURU, DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 27.01.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.4679/2012, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) dismissing the claim petition.

Brief facts:
2. On 30.06.2012 at 10.30 p.m., the deceased was going on the left side of S.M. Road,
from Kammagondanahalli towards Gangamma Circle, while so going infront of Kendriya Vidyalaya a Bajaj Scooter bearing registration No.KA-05-R-1525 driven by the 1st respondent with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased from behind and caused the accident.
Due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained head injury and other multiple injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Hospital and underwent treatment, but later on succumbed to the head injuries.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act,
claiming compensation for the death of the deceased in the accident.
The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record dismissed the claim petition.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.
5.

The Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the appellant-claimant had not produced evidence to prove that the relationship between the claimant and deceased are sister and brother.
Therefore, on this ground the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.

The Tribunal had Smt. Ramadevi vs Mr. Velu M on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72148223/
2 discussed regarding her evidence and documents placed by the claimant while deciding the relationship of the claimant and the deceased.

entities.text: Smt. Ramadevi vs Mr. Velu M
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is evidence of the claimant that the deceased is her brother.
It is stated that in the Police record, the claimant is shown as sister of the deceased.
6. Upon perusing the evidence of PW-1, PW-1 appears to be of knowing Tamil.
Hence, she put her signature in Tamil language.

Therefore, upon considering the oral and documentary evidence of the case, the Court has to give one more chance to the claimant to establish her relationship with the deceased otherwise it would be unjust.
Therefore, the case is remanded to the Tribunal without expressing any opinion on merits involved in the case.
All the contentions are kept open.
The parties are given liberty to adduce any evidence if they are so advised.

7. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is Allowed and Remanded.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 27.01.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.4679/2012, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru is setaside.
iii. The matter is remanded to the Tribunal.
The parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 01.03.2023, without expecting any further notice in this regard.
The Tribunal shall consider the matter afresh in accordance with law.
iv. The Tribunal shall hear and dispose of the matter within six months from 01.03.2023, in accordance with law.
v. The parties are at liberty to adduce further evidence and file additional material if they are so advised.
vi. The claimant is not entitled for interest from the date of filing of the appeal till today, i.e., the date of this order.
vii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
viii. No order as to costs.
